summary:
CHIRON is an AI-powered health tracking and wellbeing companion supporting astronauts from Earth-based training through space missions.

I developed this digital platform to monitor sleep, physical activity, mood, nutrition, hydration, and daily routines. It seamlessly integrates wearables including specialized medical smartwatches, actigraph wristbands, and rugged fitness trackers for continuous biometric monitoring. Combining wearable data with regular check-ins, CHIRON tracks physiological changes over time and delivers personalized wellbeing recommendations.

A core feature of CHIRON is personalized food consumption and mission supply planning. During Earth training, the system logs each astronaut’s dietary preferences, meal patterns, and exact intake quantities. By analyzing this data alongside physical activity metrics, CHIRON accurately estimates individual nutritional requirements to calculate exact launch food stocks, including emergency reserves for unexpected delays or extended missions.

Ultimately, CHIRON bridges continuous biometric health tracking with predictive food planning safeguarding astronaut wellbeing while optimizing resource management and food security for long-duration spaceflight.
details:
CHIRON – Project Details

CHIRON is an AI-powered health tracking and wellbeing companion concept designed to support astronauts from Earth-based training throughout their space missions. The project focuses on helping astronauts maintain their physical and mental wellbeing while improving mission preparation through personalized food consumption tracking and mission food supply planning.

How it works: CHIRON is designed to collect and monitor information about astronauts' sleep patterns, physical activity, mood, nutrition, hydration, food preferences, and daily routines through regular check-ins and personal records. Additionally, astronauts can connect wearable devices—including specialized medical smartwatches, actigraph wristbands, and rugged fitness trackers—for continuous biometric monitoring. By observing these patterns over time, CHIRON aims to provide personalized suggestions to help astronauts maintain healthier routines and manage their wellbeing.

An important part of the concept is its personalized food consumption and mission supply planning system. During Earth-based training, astronauts' actual food consumption, meal patterns, preferences, and quantities can be recorded alongside their physiological activity data. This information can then help estimate individual food requirements for future missions and calculate the food supplies needed for the crew. Additional emergency reserves are also considered to prepare for unexpected delays or extended missions.

Benefits and intended impact: CHIRON aims to support astronauts in maintaining better health, improving daily routines, and understanding changes in their wellbeing throughout a mission. It also supports more accurate food supply planning by using individual consumption and biometric patterns instead of relying solely on general estimates. The intended impact is to contribute to healthier astronauts, better mission preparation, improved resource management, and greater food security during long-duration space missions.

Tools and technologies used: I developed the CHIRON web application prototype using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with Visual Studio Code as my development environment. I also used AI-assisted coding tools to help with programming, debugging, and improving the application. The project is a software-based prototype that does not require proprietary hardware to run, while offering flexible support to integrate third-party wearables such as specialized medical smartwatches, actigraph wristbands, and rugged fitness trackers.

Creativity and innovation: The creative aspect of CHIRON is its combination of continuous personal health and wearable tracking with individualized food consumption analysis and mission supply planning. Rather than treating astronaut health, biometric data, and food preparation as separate areas, CHIRON brings these ideas together in one companion platform. Its main concept is to begin learning about astronauts' individual needs during Earth training and use that information to support them during future space missions.

Team and individual contribution: CHIRON was developed by me as an individual participant and solo team member. The original project idea, concept, vision, feature planning, and overall direction are entirely my own. I used AI tools as development assistants to help write and improve code, troubleshoot technical issues, and turn my concept into a working web application prototype. AI assisted with the technical development, but the idea and creative direction came solely from me.

Project considerations: While developing CHIRON, I considered usability, accessibility, personalization, astronaut wellbeing, food resource management, emergency reserves, privacy, and the challenges of long duration space missions. I also prioritized making the interface simple and understandable while ensuring that the system's recommendations support, rather than replace, qualified medical and mission guidance.

CHIRON is currently a prototype demonstrating the concept and selected features. Further development, testing, validation, and hardware integration would be required before operational deployment on space missions.
